tools.name: -health-check
tools.description: Internal health check. Verifies transport configuration (mode, which secrets are present — never their values) and, when MAIL_ACCOUNT is configured, a live JMAP session with the derived or explicit password.

tools.name: session-info
tools.description: Identity of this email instance: mailbox (MAIL_ACCOUNT), JMAP accountId, username, apiUrl, transport mode and password source (derived/user). First call to diagnose connection or credentials.

tools.name: list-folders
tools.description: Folders of this mailbox (Inbox, Sent, Drafts, Trash, …) with role, total emails and unread count. Use the returned roles as 'folder' in list-messages.

tools.name: list-messages
tools.description: List messages of a folder, most recent first, without bodies (use read-message for the content). Returns { total, offset, messages: [{ id, from, to, subject, receivedAt, seen, flagged, draft, size }] }.

folder.description: Role ('inbox', 'sent', 'drafts', 'trash', 'junk') or exact folder name. Default 'inbox'.

tools.name: read-message
tools.description: Read a message in full: headers (from/to/cc/replyTo), subject, date and body (text and HTML when present). Does not change the read state (that is mark-read).

messageId.description: Email id (the one returned by list-messages).

tools.name: send
tools.description: Send an email from this instance's mailbox (the sender is ALWAYS the configured MAIL_ACCOUNT — never a tool parameter). Draft + submit in one JMAP request; the message is stored in Sent. Confirm with the user before sending to external recipients.

to.description: Recipient address or list of addresses.

fromName.description: Display name of the sender. Default: MAIL_FROM_NAME, else the JMAP identity name.

tools.name: mark-read
tools.description: Mark messages as read or unread. Accepts a list (1..100) so a single confirmation covers the batch. Returns { updated, notUpdated }.

tools.name: destroy
tools.description: DESTROY messages permanently — irreversible, they do NOT pass through Trash. Use only with explicit user confirmation. Returns { destroyed, notDestroyed }.
